summary: Two-project integration brief: Agent Loop proposes autonomous work (README.md:53), while Tool Gate deterministically evaluates proposed tool invocations and emits allow, deny, or review_required receipts without executing them (README.md:5-20). Their shared safety boundary is the transition from agent intent to runtime side effects: proposals must not become executable authority until policy evaluation succeeds. Actionable integration: adapt every Agent Loop proposal into an InvocationEnvelope, resolve ToolMetadata from a runtime-controlled catalog, invoke Tool Gate, execute only allow receipts, route review_required to an operator, and audit denials. Agent Loop risk: a runtime path that accepts proposals directly can bypass the gate (README.md:31-33). Tool Gate risk: it consumes caller-supplied metadata and deliberately provides no authentication, authorization, or sandboxing, so an untrusted adapter could understate risk or scope and obtain an unsafe allow decision (README.md:5-13,156-158). The declared clean-tree check passed; no files were modified.
